item.title: Archive update, 2026-09-15
item.description: Classification pass: following the correction to Trayvon Martin's case, we reviewed every other case in the archive for the same issue — a genuine criminal trial that reached a final disposition without a conviction, mislabeled simply as “Unsolved.” 28 cases were reclassified to “Unresolved — No Conviction”: Isaiah Nixon, the Orangeburg Massacre (Samuel Hammond, Henry Smith & Delano Middleton), Henry “Dickie” Marrow Jr., Timothy Thomas, James T. Scott, Clinton Melton, Joseph Dumas, Samuel Younge Jr., James Earl Motley, Emmett Till, Amadou Diallo, Sean Bell, Rekia Boyd, Philando Castile, Terence Crutcher, Jonathan Ferrell, Manuel Ellis, Jahi Turner, the Clinton Avenue Five, Anthony Lamar Smith, Ta'Kiya Young, Antwon Rose II, Michael Dean, Tommie McGlothen Jr., Delrawn Small, Yvette Smith, William Green, and Freddie Gray. Four cases that surfaced in this review were deliberately left as “Unsolved” because no genuine criminal trial occurred: Willie Countryman and Maceo Snipes were each cleared only by a coroner's inquest, not a criminal trial; Breonna Taylor's own killing was never charged by any grand jury (a separate officer's federal conviction was for endangering her neighbors, not for her death); and Alteria Woods's actual shooters, three sheriff's deputies, were never charged at all — only her boyfriend was, under a different legal theory, and he was acquitted. In every case above, the underlying facts are unchanged: no one has ever been convicted.

item.title: Trayvon Martin — Case #098
item.description: Classification correction: introduced a new status, “Unresolved — No Conviction,” distinct from “Unsolved.” Trayvon Martin's case was reclassified from Unsolved to this new status, since George Zimmerman was in fact charged and tried, and a jury reached a verdict (acquittal) — unlike the majority of cases in this archive, where no charges were ever filed. The underlying facts are unchanged: the medical examiner's homicide finding stands, and no one has ever been convicted in Martin's death. This correction was prompted by a reader.
